_what: What the 1-ARGUMENT form of `ta.highest` / `ta.lowest` defaults its SOURCE to, read off a live TradingView chart.
_why_it_matters: ⭐⭐ THE 81-SITE QUESTION. `docs/pine/r11-group-b-arity.md` names the risk exactly: "does `ta.highest(20)` default the source to `high` (and `ta.lowest` to `low`), or to `close` for both? The asymmetry is the whole risk — guessing `close` would be silently wrong on 81 sites." It is an asymmetry, and it is now measured rather than assumed.
_ruling: ⭐ `ta.highest(n)` DEFAULTS TO `high`. `ta.lowest(n)` DEFAULTS TO `low`. Not `close` for either, and not `hl2`. 397 of 397 usable bars agree, with ZERO bars agreeing with any rival reading.
_instrument: UCTPROBE_GB_HILO (Script$USER;86a18d10d3f145e48b4bae17fef98ffe), added to the chart from the Pine editor with the action button asserted to read "Add to chart" and no "Update on chart" present. Buffer verified sha256-identical to the committed source before the click: bc77f04a2cca668a9e43da8886940255b0fde7bcb0d94d22f96ec86418865e8e, 3502 characters.
_gates: isFailed() === false; plot roster 11 == the balanced-paren scan of the committed source; 400 bars with values.
_the_discriminators_own_discriminator: ⛔ N02 AND N03 COULD BOTH HAVE READ 0 IF `high` AND `close` HAPPENED TO AGREE OVER THE WINDOW, and the probe would have looked conclusive while answering nothing. N06/N07 are the spread between the explicit forms and MUST be non-zero on any bar a verdict is read from; 3 of the 400 bars fail that guard (the warmup, where the window is not yet full) and are EXCLUDED from the tally rather than counted. That is why the denominator is 397 and not 400.

agreementCounts._: bars (of 397 usable) on which the 1-arg form equals the named explicit form

_bounds: ⚠️ ONE SYMBOL, ONE TIMEFRAME, ONE SESSION. It establishes the DEFAULT SOURCE, which is a property of the function signature rather than of SPY — a default that varied by instrument would be a far stranger finding than the one under test. It says nothing about the 2-argument form (never in doubt) or about `ta.highestbars`/`ta.lowestbars`, whose own defaulting is a separate question this probe does not ask.
_what_our_engine_must_do: ⚰️ THE ENGINE DOES NOT MATCH THIS YET, AND THE GAP IS PINNED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. A 1-arg `ta.highest(n)` should resolve its source to `high` and `ta.lowest(n)` to `low`; today the door answers `pine:arity` for both, on 97 one-argument sites across 33 files (measured by balanced-paren scan over all 510 tracked .pine files; the doc's older figure of 81 is stale and understated). ⛔ THE FIX WAS WRITTEN AND REVERTED THE SAME NIGHT: supplying the default via `PINE_NAMESPACED_TREE` also RECLASSIFIES the names, because `pineRuntimeFrontend.js`'s `windowTarget` and `carriedTarget` both treat membership of that map as "not a carried/windowed builtin" — so the runtime lane started refusing `runtime:call-windowed-state` for the TWO-argument form, which had always worked. The default belongs where ARITY is resolved, a facility this engine does not have. ⭐ `app/src/components/chart/engine/ast/pine.hiloDefault.test.js` reads THIS file for the vendor half and pins the refusal for the engine half; `requests.md` carries the routed fix.
